newsitem.title: GERMANY: ATHLETICS-EAA BACK PROPOSALS FOR TWO-YEAR DRUG BAN.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-EAA BACK PROPOSALS FOR TWO-YEAR DRUG BAN.

text.p: The European Athletic Association (EAA) said on Sunday that they would back International Amateur Athletic Federation's proposals to reduce bans for doping offences to two years.
The current length of the ban for serious doping offences is four years but national laws in several leading athletics nations, including Germany, prevent the full ban being imposed.
Carl Olaf Homen, EAA president, said that the decision by the EAA council had been unanimous.
"Two years ago in Gothenburg the EAA support was divided (for reducing the ban to two years) but the situation has changed."
"Many countries, owing to their national laws, do not have the possibility to implement a four-year ban."
"In reality we must have the same ban in all countries."
Homen also announced that there were three candidates to stage the 2002 European championships -- Amsterdam, Lausanne and Munich.
A decision will be made on October 9.
